decisive_items: A 61-year-old man with a 20-year history of recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation, alternating with intermittent diarrhea
exploratory laparotomy “showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions.”
CT scan showed small-bowel dilation (approximately 23 mm in diameter) consistent with obstruction and a concurrent megacolon dilated up to 15 cm
response.rationale: Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction is supported by recurrent obstructive symptoms without mechanical cause, bowel dilation on imaging, and secondary fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption; R5 is the same entity but lacks the supported chronic qualifier.

rejected.why: Celiac disease was excluded by endoscopy showing no evidence and by lack of response to a gluten-free diet.
Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies are nonspecific and there is no evidence of lymphatic dilation or protein-losing enteropathy.
Alcohol history is present but no liver-specific findings; symptoms worsened after alcohol cessation and obstruction is unexplained.
No bowel resection is described to cause short bowel syndrome; weight loss and vitamin deficiencies are secondary to the motility/malabsorptive process.
